blocks.text: Cloud computing is a technology that allows users to store, manage, and process data on remote servers instead of local computers (as shown in Figure 8.4). These servers are hosted on the internet and managed by cloud service providers. This means users can access their data and applications anytime, from anywhere, using an internet connection. The cloud eliminates the need for powerful personal computers, as most of the processing is done remotely.

By using cloud computing, individuals and businesses can use online services such as data storage, web hosting, and software applications without having to maintain physical hardware. It supports modern digital tools like streaming platforms, online learning systems, and collaborative workspaces. This technology forms the backbone of many services people use daily, making computing more flexible and connected.

blocks.title: Do You Know?
blocks.text: When you save a document on Google Drive or iCloud, you're actually using Cloud Computing.
